This rare event, known as a tidal disruption event, was first detected in November 2025 by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) as an unusual brightening in a galaxy about 750 million light-years away. Further observations by NASA’s Swift confirmed the event, revealing a black hole weighing about a million times the mass of the Sun, located far from the galaxy’s core.

### Significance of the Discovery

This discovery is significant because it challenges previous assumptions that supermassive black holes are always found at the centers of galaxies. The black hole responsible for this event may have originated in a galaxy’s core but was ejected due to gravitational interactions, or it may have come from a dwarf galaxy that merged with the host galaxy. The findings, published in *The Astrophysical Journal Letters*, validate a new technique for identifying such events and could help astronomers better understand the distribution and movement of supermassive black holes in the universe.

### Future of the Swift Mission
